To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) similarity solutions of the entrainment flow problem with finite mass and momentum flux exist, (2) the similarity models can be used to describe the entrainment flow in a wide range of the Reynolds numbers and for the flow with the competitive influence of mass and momentum, (3) the mass-dominated similarity solution can be used to predict the flow velocity and the denuded zone width in the selective laser melting.
we theoretically found new similarity solutions of the entrainment flow with the finite mass and momentum flux and no characteristic length.
we theoretically studied the entrainment flow in the vicinity of a jet emerging from a wall into a half-space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of similarity flows, namely, with the entrainment flow emerging from a plane surface into a half-space.
the development of a new approach to similarity modeling of viscous flows with the no-sleep boundary conditions.
the entrainment flow in the vicinity of a jet emerging from a flat surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entrainment flow model with the no-slack boundary condition is a promising tool for the analysis of the entrainment flow and evaporation at the selective laser melting process.
the entrainment flow model is valid at the jet Reynolds numbers Re = 30, 50 and 80, and the mass-dominated model is valid at Re = 30.
the entrainment flow is dominated by mass flux and the entrainment flow model can be used to describe the entrainment flow for the jet emerging from the surface of the substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the theory for the entrainment flow in the vicinity of the jet origin.
we have found similarity solutions of the problem of the jet entrainment flow and have applied them to the problem of laser-induced evaporation.
the developed methods and results are useful for the analysis and design of microfluidic devices and for the study of the entrainment flows of viscous jets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entrainment flow can be described by similarity models, which are applicable to a broad range of Reynolds numbers.
the entrainment flow is a complex process, which is determined by the competition of the mass and the momentum fluxes.
the entrainment flow in a half space is described by similarity solutions that can be used to evaluate the flow parameters and wall stresses in the jet region and to predict the jet behavior.
